To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the number of messages sent over the network in a multi-hop Byzantine reliable broadcast algorithm is not exponential, and (b) it is possible to design a Byzantine reliable broadcast protocol that has a message complexity that is linear in the number of nodes in the network, and that is also robust against Byzantine nodes.

We revisit Byzantine Reliable Broadcast algorithms in multi-hop wireless networks and propose a set of optimizations that preserve their safety and liveness while decreasing their observed message complexities by up to 2 orders of magnitude.
we propose a new reliable broadcast algorithm that is Byzantine fault tolerant and has a message complexity that is significantly better than previous solutions.

, in practice, Byzantine-tolerating reliable broadcast can be implemented using only a small constant factor more messages than the number of nodes in the network, and that the constant factor is independent of the number of Byzantine nodes.
